## Practical Notes on the Demos

Beyond the compute ceiling above, three things actually bite:

- The first weight download often takes longer than the inference itself, so the notebook has to be warmed up before class.
- A few dozen utterances from LibriSpeech `dev-clean` plus MUSAN are enough; there is no reason to touch a large dataset.
- The six "play the broken one first" demos are the most memorable part of the course: Griffin-Lim phase reconstruction (W2), the CTC blank posterior heatmap (W3), Whisper hallucination (W7), vocoder artifacts (W8), WER going *up* after enhancement (W10), and barging in versus responding too slowly (W12).
